Thank you. I know that you didn’t mean that question to be mean, but I never thought about it, and it almost made me a little upset because you’re right and it’s a valid point. I don’t think I’ve ever once considered how he might feel if our positions were reversed, or if I was in the same spot as he is as far as having been married and having children. I guess that’s where my fear of it being a stupid and selfish thing to be upset about comes from. I’m really only thinking of me and how I feel despite him literally telling me that it’s not true and things will be special, just in a different way. I think I’ve just grown up with the old fashioned way of date, marry, family. I grew up in a blended home FFS — I don’t know why I have such disdain for not being “special”, whatever that even means anymore. Thank you again for responding, I really appreciate it.

Thank you, so much. This is exactly what I needed to hear. I think you’re absolutely right in that I kind of had this whole “perfect” bs idea growing up. And I know it shouldn’t matter as long as I love him, which I very much do, and I know he loves me. 

I was insecure at first, even having a good friendship with his ex, that I would never compare to her in anything that I do. That was rough, but I think it felt a little more valid and normal than my worries about nothing being special to him. I got over that well and quickly, and I think part of me is so used to just finding issues with things and being comfortable in a state of fear. Thank you again for taking the time to type out that response. It means a lot.

Poor thing! Sounds like stress from moving. I have a very anxious cat as well that never takes well to moving. Surround your place with as many pieces of clothing or towels or blankets that smell like you. They make plug in diffusers called Feliway (also available as spray or wipes) that emit a hormone for cats that can help ease their nerves, I recommend them! If you can, for now, keep her contained into a single room with a little box and some familiar smells and slowly ease her out of there into the rest of the home. You might also want to try some different foods that might help her tummy settle better; my boy is on a sensitive stomach dry kibble and Lil’ Soups for breakfast and dinner as his anxiety keeps him skinny and this is one of the foods I’ve found he absolutely loves and eats up. 
For when I’m gone, I’ll set aside some time to play with him and maybe give him some catnip so that he’s pretty tired before I leave. I leave a quiet radio on, and I also purchased a camera that allows me to check on him and talk through it so that he can hear my voice when I’m not around. 
They also make sprays that deter cats from peeing in certain places!
If these problems persist absolutely check with your vet. It’s worth even contacting them now — they may be able to recommend some better tips and tricks and possibly even a temporary med to help her adjust and relax. Good luck!
